key_headlines.title: Korea and US Launch Mega AI Alliance to Counter China's Tech Advances
key_headlines.summary: South Korean tech giants including Samsung, SK, Hyundai, and Naver partnered with US tech companies at an AI Summit to establish a massive AI semiconductor and physical AI business partnership, countering China's rapid AI development.

key_headlines.title: Government to Announce Housing Finance Measures and Tax Reforms Soon
key_headlines.summary: The Financial Services Commission pledged to announce comprehensive housing finance measures and tax reform plans shortly, including strengthened property taxes on ultra-luxury and non-residential single homes while maintaining overall loan volume management.

key_headlines.title: South Korea Hit with 12.5% Forced Labor Tariff from United States
key_headlines.summary: The Trump administration imposed a 12.5% tariff on Korea under the Forced Labor Tariff Act, replacing the previous 10% global tariff, affecting major export sectors including semiconductors, batteries, automobiles, and shipbuilding.

key_headlines.title: Q2 GDP Growth Surges to 0.6% Quarter-on-Quarter, Exceeding Expectations
key_headlines.summary: Korea's second quarter real GDP growth reached 0.6% quarter-on-quarter, triple the central bank's 0.2% forecast and nearly matching Q1's 1.9%, putting annual 3% growth target within reach.

key_headlines.title: Apartment Prices Surge: Average Nationwide Jeonse Price Breaks 21 Million Won Per 3.3 Sqm
key_headlines.summary: National average apartment selling prices hit a record 21.43 million won per 3.3 square meters in the first half of 2026, marking the first time breaking the 21 million won threshold.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea and the United States unveiled a massive AI semiconductor and physical AI partnership involving major Korean tech companies to counter China's technological advances. The government announced plans to release comprehensive housing finance measures and property tax reforms shortly, including strengthened taxes on ultra-luxury and non-residential single homes. The second quarter GDP growth reached 0.6% quarter-on-quarter, significantly exceeding forecasts and supporting potential annual 3% growth. The US imposed a 12.5% forced labor tariff on Korea alongside 60 other countries, affecting major export sectors. These developments signal both opportunities in AI collaboration and challenges from increased protectionist trade measures.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Korea's Q2 real GDP growth reached 0.6% quarter-on-quarter, triple the central bank's 0.2% forecast, supporting expectations for 3% annual growth and potential GNI reaching 40,000 dollars. However, concerns about 'jobless growth' persist as employment gains lag economic expansion. Interest rate hike expectations intensified following stronger-than-expected GDP data, with market-implied probabilities for August and September rate increases rising significantly. Public sector wage negotiations are underway, with unions demanding 7.1% increases to recover real wage losses. Core inflation trends will be critical in determining the central bank's monetary policy path forward.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market experienced significant volatility with KOSPI plunging over 5% amid Middle East tensions and surging oil prices exceeding $100 per barrel. Major semiconductor stocks including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix declined 7-8% as rising international oil prices fueled inflation concerns and pushed US Treasury yields to 18-month highs. Sell-side circuit breakers were triggered in both KOSPI and KOSDAQ markets as foreign and institutional investors turned net sellers while retail investors provided support. US equity weakness, particularly in technology stocks, spilled over into Korean markets, with Nasdaq declining approximately 2%. Single-stock leveraged ETFs continued drawing scrutiny as a potential contributor to market volatility.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's technology sector received a boost from the new US-Korea AI partnership announced at the presidential AI Summit, promoting collaboration in HBM semiconductors and physical AI robotics technology. The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment announced the second semiconductor fabrication plant in Honam region will begin operations by end of 2029, with renewable energy systems addressing intermittency challenges. Korea faces a 12.5% forced labor tariff from the US, though major export sectors like semiconductors, shipbuilding, and batteries remain crucial negotiations. The biotech sector is expected to rival semiconductors within a decade under government support for red, white, and green biotech integration. Intel reported strong Q2 results with 25% revenue growth driven by AI data center demand, signaling continued semiconductor sector strength.
sections.Real Estate: The government announced imminent release of comprehensive property tax and income tax reform measures targeting ultra-luxury homes and non-residential single-home owners while providing relief for actual residents. National average apartment selling prices hit a record 21.43 million won per 3.3 square meters in H1 2026, marking the first break above 21 million won. Property tax will employ differential taxation based on price, use, and location, with strengthened burdens on speculation and investment properties while easing taxes on primary residences. The government plans to streamline procedures for the third new town projects and relax loan requirements for reconstruction and redevelopment relocation. Debate continues between the central government and Seoul regarding the supply effects of reconstruction and redevelopment projects.
sections.International Economy: Middle East tensions escalated, pushing international crude oil prices toward $100 per barrel and triggering global market volatility, with US 10-year Treasury yields rising to 4.7%. The US imposed 12.5% forced labor tariffs on Korea, Japan, and Australia while implementing 10-12.5% tariffs on 60 countries, effectively replacing the previous 10% global tariff. Japan joined Korea in expressing regret over the forced labor tariff designation despite compliance with international norms. US Federal Reserve rate hike probabilities increased significantly, with markets pricing in 80% odds for September and 92% for December increases. The Trump administration established the Korea-US Shipbuilding Cooperation Center, signaling continued sectoral collaboration despite broader trade tensions.
sections.AI & Economy: Intel reported second quarter revenue of $16.1 billion, a 25% year-on-year increase driven by surging AI data center demand, marking the strongest growth since 2011 and exceeding market expectations. Google's parent company Alphabet recorded its first negative free cash flow in Q2 due to massive AI infrastructure investments, yet committed to spending an additional 22 trillion won on AI development this year. South Korea's data center sector attracted interest from major corporations, with Samcheok emerging as a competitive location due to superior power supply efficiency and available land for AI data centers. The biotech sector is positioned to challenge semiconductors within a decade through AI-integrated drug development platforms. Global tech companies like Blackstone expanded from data centers into power and credit platforms to support AI infrastructure expansion.
sections.Others: Domestic pharmaceutical companies are being supported to shift from generic drugs to high-value blockbuster drugs with annual revenues exceeding 1.5 trillion won through customized AI and data support. Kia reported record Q2 revenue of 33 trillion won despite a 4.9% operating profit decline, though operating margins improved sequentially to 8% following recent US tariff impacts. Nicaragua's authoritarian political declaration raised concerns about US coffee prices, as the country supplies 35% of US coffee bean imports and prices already reached 16-year highs. Blackstone pivoted from traditional real estate to become a major AI infrastructure financier, managing 550 billion dollars in assets and planning 10 billion dollars in private credit supply. ChatGPT and other generative AI systems mention Japan most frequently in responses across 24 languages, suggesting potential AI-driven preference for Japanese content and products.
